reviews.decision_reason: demand_selection treats every supplied corpus row with demand_score >= 3 as demand-backed and only adds hard-coded fallback ids. The supplied package contains score/need/source metadata but no observed jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, or outcomes, so this unit lets unsupported market-demand claims pass through as selected needs. That is behaviorally significant because downstream recommendation depends on these selected records.

evidence_normalization whitelists record ids and normalizes columns, but it does not validate whether evidence actually supports market demand under the required criteria. Missing demand evidence remains hidden because all eight records are retained as normalized needs despite the absence of observed-job/customer-demand support in the supplied input.

provenance_assembly ranks retained rows by demand_score and record_id, presenting them as evidence_sources even though the package supplies only source ids/weights and no underlying customer-demand observations. This gives unsupported rows provenance ranks that downstream uses to prioritize unsupported need n06-r01, so the missing evidence is behaviorally significant rather than merely cosmetic.
